subject: [PATCH v3] kernfs: allocate inodes and dentry outside kernfs_rwsem

2026-10-16.patch_summary: This patch addresses long stalls in kernfs due to allocation of inodes and dentries while holding the kernfs_rwsem lock, which can lead to memory reclaim delays and OOM killer activations. The patch allocates inodes outside the lock and frees them if unused, similar to previous commits for other use cases. This change reduces wait times in various scenarios, including cgroupfs operations, and improves overall system performance.

reviews.author: Jori Koolstra
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Jori Koolstra noted that mentioning memcg is unnecessary and not relevant to understanding the patch, and complimented the author on implementing a similar solution in another series.

Reviewer Jori Koolstra expressed concern about the complexity of the kernfs_iop_lookup() function's contract, questioning whether an output parameter is truly necessary for such a simple function.

reviewer questioned the correctness of removing locking in kernfs_get_tree(), expressing uncertainty about potential serialization issues

Reviewer noted that the patch does not actually allocate inodes and dentry outside kernfs_rwsem as claimed, but instead only moves kernfs_get_parent_dentry() to hold the lock around inode lookup
reviews.raw_body:
I wouldn't mention memcg here per se, it is not relevant to grasp its
use. In another series I have implemented almost the same thing (but you
did it better!).

---

I understand this is intended to have some kind of ownership semantics,
but I must say for such a simple function, I find the contract quite
complex to check. Do we really need an out parameter here?

---

What are you serializing against here? I've been looking at this as well
recently, and I thought we could just get rid of the locking here. But
on second look, I am not so sure what is correct.

Is there anything that serializes kernfs_get_tree() with root node
removal?

---

Thanks,
Jori.

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that the kernfs_rwsem lock is still held during inode allocation in kernfs_fill_super(), agreed to restructure in a future version.

The author acknowledged that the current implementation of iput(new) without a check is not ideal, agreed to restructure it in a similar way to inode_insert5(), and promised to let the caller do the necessary check before calling iput().

Author acknowledged a concern about the kernfs_fill_super change and agreed to drop it from their patch, suggesting that Jori Koolstra's earlier patch will cover this issue better.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Jori and thanks a lot for taking a look.

On Sun, Oct 18, 2026 at 10:47:56PM +0200, Jori Koolstra wrote:

---

Not really. I just used it simply call iput(new) without a check. I can change
it and make it more like inode_insert5() and let caller do check before calling
iput().

---

That is a good question and honestly I didn't know the answer. After digging a
bit, I think 07/12 patch [1] of your series is right.

Superblock is still private here and it is added to the supers list after
kernfs_fill_super. Root removal is not serialized by kernfs and kernfs users
keep the root alive across the mount.

I can drop the kernfs_fill_super change from my patch and I think your patch
will cover it better.

[1] https://lore.kernel.org/20261016143806.2946578-8-jkoolstra@xs4all.nl

reviews.author: Jori Koolstra
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Jori Koolstra expressed concerns that the patch does not provide a way to allocate an inode before calling scops->mkdir, which is necessary for error handling in case of memory allocation failure. They suggested creating a new function kernfs_get_inode_locked_fast() or replicating the structure of iget5_locked(), and also recommended using alloc_inode() instead of new_inode().

Reviewer Jori Koolstra expressed uncertainty about the claim that preallocating the root inode outside kernfs_rwsem eliminates inode allocation under this lock for all kernfs users, requesting verification.

The reviewer noted that the patch does not address the issue of kernfs_iop_lookup() holding kernfs_rwsem across memcg reclaim, which can lead to long stalls in cgroupfs.
reviews.raw_body:
I'd prefer no out parameter then. I actually need the same function, more or less.
My problem is that I want inode allocation before calling scops->mkdir, so that
if that goes -ENOMEM, then we don't create the directory. However, since I can
expect that there's not going to be an inode present, the ilookup is not needed.
So I guess I need a kernfs_get_inode_locked_fast() or something.

But also, shouldn't we just replicate the structure of iget5_locked() here? Except
that we pass in an allocated inode. We invoke a lot more code if we rely on iput()
instead of destroy_inode(). Then maybe we need to use alloc_inode() instead of
new_inode() as well.

---

I am not sure that last statement is true for all kernfs users. I will have to
verify.

---

Best,
Jori.
